purpose: Evidence that the frontend consumes the published backend vocabulary and nothing else, and that it is truthful against BOTH trees: protected main (no publication) and agent-2's publication (fb254f32).

protectedMain.note: this branch carries a copy of the protected-main backend; neither ai.context nor ai.agent-session is locked here

protectedMainBlock.note: protected main publishes both contracts, so the surface derives published and renders version 1.0.0

publishedOnPeerBranchBlock.commitMessage: Implement P2.13 context and session foundation

rows.notes: P2.13 smallest additive publication from the already-declared ai.context fields and Context & Session operation vocabulary. The implementation is bounded local state only: no model/provider/runtime dependency, no transcript dump, no Memory store. Contract lock publication does not make P2.13 complete; Manager reconciliation, merge validation and post-merge verification remain required.

P2.13 smallest additive publication from the established ai.agent-session fields and states. A session is bounded identity/control state with references, never an unbounded transcript. The implementation remains provider/runtime-neutral.

publishedOnPeerBranchBlock.consumedBy: packages/frontend-lego/src/vocabulary.mjs (quoted sets contextOperation, continuationSection, contextRolloverPhase, continuationVerification) and packages/frontend-lego/test/29-alignment.test.mjs
publishedOnPeerBranchBlock.atMerge: when the manager merges the publication into protected main, `rows` above moves into `publication.rows` and `status` becomes `published` in the same change; test/32 asserts that against the default tree

publicationManifest.policy: publication.rows carries only what THIS tree publishes, so the surface cannot claim a publication it does not hold; the peer rows are evidence, recorded verbatim, in a separate block.

openDecisions.question: Which contract rows and which rollover/continuation vocabulary does the manager publish for Context & Session, so the frontend binds to a lock row instead of to a version claim?

The frontend evidence capture pins descriptor assembly at under 4,096 KB of heap; P2.12 filled that pin to 3,780 KB (92%) and the P2.13 Context & Session surface adds ~470 KB, so the check now fails at 4,251-4,361 KB. Does the manager raise the pin, make feature surfaces opt-in imports instead of eager assembly, or move surface prose into the manifests - and which of those applies to P2.14 (Memory), which cannot fit under the pin as it stands?

Pre-existing at e754c5df, environmental, not a code regression.
